doc.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Every gig counts; formative moments
summary: No single breakthrough gig; camp, David Garibaldi's groove, and listening to Ray Brown walk.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So what was your first, what you consider to be a gig or a series of gigs where you really got to pull it all together, and kind of use everything you’d learned up to that point?

Every gig. There’s no one gig. I mean there’s some where you play with better people than others but every gig is important. Every gig that I play and have ever played is using everything that I’ve been learning up to that point. Because you’re always trying to make the best music that you can. Of course I mean there’s like a whole series of things. When I was a kid just being able to go and sing at that jazz camp. That was huge for me. That was life changing. Playing bass in an ensemble at the college that I went to with David Garibaldi, the first time I really felt a solid groove. It was just like — uhhhh.
Oh is that the fella, he’s in Tower of Power?

Yeah. And it was like a funk set. But it was like one of those things where I actually felt a solid groove. It was the first time I’d every played with — but it was just like oh this feels really good. You know, it’s just little moments like that, I mean they keep encouraging you. Or sometimes it was not even playing at all but just being, sitting there in a room listening to Ray Brown play a walking bass line. You know don’t even have him solo, just to have him walk in the medium Ray Brown groove. I mean it was just — there are a series of things that are really important like that, but I think every gig is important. It doesn’t matter if it’s in a restaurant, a hotel, at a jazz party like this. Every one of them demands, the music demands that you play your best and use everything that you’ve learned up to that point.
